title: Leaf Wetness Fungus Risk Watch
dataSources: Weather-station observations (`ecowitt:obs`, `weatherflow:obs`), air-quality readings (`purpleair:aqi`, `airgradient:sensor`), soil-moisture and greenhouse sensors (`plant:sensor`), aquarium controllers (`aquarium:sensor`).
app: Personal weather stations (Ecowitt/Ambient/Davis/WeatherFlow), air-quality sensors (PurpleAir/AirGradient), and aquarium/greenhouse/soil sensors via HEC and MQTT.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=plant:sensor
| stats avg(leaf_wetness_pct) as wetness, avg(humidity_pct) as humidity by zone
| where wetness>80 AND humidity>85
| sort - wetness
description: Looks for persistently wet, humid plant zones where mildew, blight, or fungus pressure is likely to rise.
value: Many garden diseases thrive in exactly this damp microclimate; a simple threshold helps you intervene early with airflow or pruning.
implementation: Forward leaf-wetness and humidity signals where available; review hot spots daily during high-risk seasons.
visualization: Zone table of leaf wetness and humidity with risk status.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces which parts of the garden are staying wet and humid enough that fungus problems could start growing.
